chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: The time of Maghrib is when the redness disappears from the east. Do you know how that is? I said: No. He said: Because the east overlooks the west like this, and he raised his right hand above his left; so when it disappears from here, the redness departs from here.

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the reddish glow remaining in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib prayer time at sunset
key_terms.غَابَتْ: disappeared or went out of sight
key_terms.مُطِلٌّ: overlooking or appearing above in relation to
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the designated time or appointed onset of an act

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Maghrib begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the beginning time of Maghrib by the disappearance of the eastern redness after sunset. It presents a legal indicator for determining prayer time and clarifies it through a physical gesture and brief explanation.
